title: PostgreSQL Optimization for Multi-Billion Row Tables: Monthly Partitioning & BRIN Indexes
summary: Partitioning strategy for massive audit/event tables and utilizing Block Range Indexes (BRIN) to cut index memory footprint by 95% compared to conventional B-Trees.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.business-data-requirements: User telemetry and GPS tracking systems logged over 2 billion rows annually. When table size exceeded 500GB, traditional B-Tree indexes consumed 120GB of RAM, exceeding database buffer cache and causing severe analytical query degradation.
sections.data-modeling:
Relational partitioning architecture:

  • Declarative Partitioning: Splitting the primary table by monthly time ranges via PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at).
  • Partition Pruning: Allowing the PostgreSQL query planner to completely bypass non-relevant child tables during range filter evaluations.
sections.pipeline-construction:
Implementing Block Range Indexes (BRIN):

  • Because time-series data is written monotonically in ascending physical block order, BRIN only tracks min/max summaries per 128 disk pages (pages_per_range = 128).
  • Automated upcoming month partition creation using the pg_partman extension.
sections.testing-optimization: Performance gains: Total index size plummeted from 120GB to just 450MB (over 99% reduction). Range scan throughput accelerated by 5x due to precise Partition Pruning.
sections.summary-recommendations: BRIN indexes are ideal for append-only time-series datasets in PostgreSQL. Recommendation: Schedule periodic VACUUM ANALYZE maintenance to preserve BRIN block metadata accuracy.

title: End-to-End Distributed Tracing with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus and Grafana for Spring Boot
summary: Tracking distributed request lifecycles across microservice clusters, diagnosing latency bottlenecks, and rendering live Service Dependency Graphs.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.article-objectives: Establish a comprehensive Observability ecosystem for Spring Boot microservices, enabling engineering teams to identify and resolve distributed latency spikes within minutes.
sections.architecture-principles:
Unified three pillars of Observability (Tracing, Metrics, Logs):

  • OpenTelemetry Java Agent: Automatically injects and propagates Trace and Span IDs across asynchronous HTTP calls via W3C Trace Context headers.
  • OpenTelemetry Collector: Ingests telemetry, sanitizes sensitive parameters, and routes data to Prometheus and Grafana Tempo.
  • Grafana Dashboard: Visualizes live Service Dependency Graphs and facilitates seamless jumps from Metric Alerts directly into correlated Traces.
sections.step-by-step-setup:
Configuration details:

  • Step 1: Attach opentelemetry-javaagent.jar inside the production Spring Boot Dockerfile.
  • Step 2: Set environment variable OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317.
  • Step 3: Configure Prometheus alert rules utilizing the RED method (Rate, Errors, Duration).
sections.troubleshooting-pitfalls:
• Context Propagation Loss in Async Threads: Occurs when switching threads without wrapping Context.current(). Fixed via custom Spring TaskDecorators.
  • Network Bandwidth Bloat: Configure Tail-based Sampling on Otel Collector to capture 100% of error traces while sampling only 5% of healthy traces.
sections.evaluation-scaling: Decreased Mean Time to Detection (MTTD) and Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) from 45 minutes down to under 3 minutes across production fleets.

title: Mastering Advanced TypeScript: Discriminated Unions, Type Guards and Generic Constraints in Practice
summary: Leveraging TypeScript's expressive type system to eliminate impossible UI states at compile-time and design rock-solid Type-Safe application interfaces.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.problem-statement: In complex frontend applications, managing asynchronous state using fragmented boolean flags (isLoading, hasError, data) inevitably yields impossible states (e.g. rendering both loading spinner and error alert simultaneously).
sections.initial-approach: Naive approaches often resort to any or unsafe as Type assertions, circumventing TypeScript's safety guarantees entirely.
sections.optimization-thinking:
Model application state with Discriminated Unions:

  • Every state variant possesses a single discriminator property (e.g. status: 'success' | 'error').
  • Custom Type Guards provide foolproof, safe type narrowing.
  • Apply the never type for exhaustive compile-time pattern matching.
sections.code-implementation:
Type-safe asynchronous state management:

type AsyncState =
  | { status: 'idle' }
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { status: 'success'; data: T }
  | { status: 'error'; error: Error };

function renderState(state: AsyncState) {
  switch (state.status) {
    case 'success': return renderUser(state.data);
    case 'error': return renderError(state.error);
    case 'loading': return ;
    case 'idle': return null;
  }
}
sections.complexity-applications: Eliminated 100% of runtime Cannot read properties of undefined exceptions and elevated engineering velocity through rich IDE IntelliSense autocomplete.

title: System Design Interview Playbook for Senior & Lead: 4-Step Framework and Trade-off Mental Models
summary: Essential guide to mastering large-scale system design interviews: From clarifying ambiguities and back-of-the-envelope calculations to rigorous trade-off evaluations.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.introduction: System design interviews evaluate an engineer's technical depth, structured problem solving, and practical trade-off intuition. This guide distills learnings from evaluating dozens of Senior and Lead candidates.
sections.multi-dimensional-evaluation:
Standard 4-step framework for tackling system design challenges:

  • Step 1: Clarify Scope & Requirements: Delineate functional vs non-functional constraints (QPS, DAU, latency SLA, consistency models).
  • Step 2: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation: Calculate read/write throughput, 5-year storage capacity, and network egress bandwidth.
  • Step 3: High-Level Architecture: Diagram end-to-end data flows from Client -> CDN / API Gateway -> Microservices -> Cache -> Database.
  • Step 4: Deep Dive & Bottlenecks: Address single points of failure, partition sharding schemes, and CAP theorem consistency boundaries.
sections.case-study-experience: URL Shortener case study: Rather than immediately pitching Redis or Kafka, exceptional candidates first calculate the Read:Write ratio (100:1) to mathematically justify the caching layer.
sections.actionable-recommendations: There are no silver bullets in distributed systems. Always proactively articulate the trade-offs of your chosen architectural decisions.
sections.open-questions-discussion: What was the most challenging system design interview scenario you have encountered? What architectural trade-offs stood out?
